text:
sara: Hey team, seeing a new nodepool scale-up where GPU nodes come up but end up NotReady/NoSchedule. cluster-autoscaler keeps adding nodes and costs spike :grimacing:
sara: kubectl describe node gpu-pool-27 shows KubeletNotReady + taint: node.kubernetes.io/not-ready:NoSchedule
sara: Device plugin isn't registering, logs show handshake timeout. snippet:
```
I0315 12:34:01.123456 1 main.go:85] Starting device plugin
E0315 12:34:12.234567 1 plugin.go:210] handshake with kubelet failed: timeout waiting for response
```
sara: dmesg on node shows a few GPU errors too:
```
[  10.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:00:01): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
[  10.124000] nvidia: failed to register with kernel module
```
max: ugh. are these preemptible VMs again? noisy kernels from images?
max: quick checks: `kubectl get pods -n kube-system -o wide | grep nvidia` and `kubectl logs -n kube-system nvidia-device-plugin-xxxx`
liam: saw similar last month when image/kernel got rolled. We had driver module mismatch so nvidia-smi failed and plugin exited. Could be node image updated without matching driver bundle.
sara: confirmed nodes are on image gpunode-2026-03-12 vs driver package expecting 2026-02. Also these nodes are in us-west2b which we recently bumped autoscale in to save cost with preemptible pool.
infra-bot: Alert: 6 new NotReady GPU nodes detected in us-west2b (gpu-pool). Escalation channel: #eng-infra.
max: short term: mark GPU nodepool with `--max-unavailable=0` for rolling updates? or set node taint tolerant on pending pods so autoscaler won't keep adding?
liam: autoscaler is seeing pods pending with `nvidia.com/gpu` requests, so it keeps adding nodes. But because nodes don't register, pods remain pending -> feedback loop. We need to stop autoscaler or add a temporary capacity buffer.
sara: I'm going to scale down autoscaler by setting max nodes to current to stop new nodes from coming up: `kubectl patch cm cluster-autoscaler -n kube-system --type merge -p '{"data":{"max-nodes":"10"}}'` (we use a configmap wrapper)
max: also recommend cordoning faulty nodes so draining doesn't try to move GPU workloads into them: `kubectl cordon gpu-pool-27`
liam: root cause options: kernel version mismatch / cloud image missing nvidia kernel module / device-plugin timeout too short. We should also look at kubelet logs: `journalctl -u kubelet | grep device-plugin`
sara: logs show repeated `failed to create device plugin: no devices found` and `permission denied` from /dev/nvidiactl on some nodes. suspect udev or init ordering race.
max: One mitigation: add `systemd` drop-in to start nvidia-persistenced earlier and set device-plugin restartPolicy=always with backoff. Might be safer to bake driver into image or use driver container that loads module before kubelet.
liam: Agreed. For long term: 1) Bake matching nvidia driver into node image + validate during image build. 2) Increase device-plugin handshake timeout to 60s. 3) Add startup probe in daemonset to avoid readiness before device is present. 4) Update cluster-autoscaler to respect node startup time (increase `--scale-up-delay`) and enable `expander=least-waste`.
sara: Also cost note: preemptible nodes reduce $ but introduce more churn - our current scaling policy has aggressive scale-up which amplifies failures into cost. We should cap burst capacity for GPU pools.
max: For this incident, I restarted the device-plugin daemonset on one failing node after enabling the correct nvidia modules; it then registered and pods scheduled. Rolling fix: create a job to validate module presence on new nodes and taint nodes `NoSchedule` until validated.
sara: I'll open a short RFC for: bake drivers in image + add node init check + autoscaler safeguards. tagging @liam to help with autoscaler flags.
liam: I'll also add a temporary autoscaler policy to reduce churn in us-west2b and add alerting on repeated device-plugin handshake failures (>=3 per hour).
max: 👍 Also let's document the exact commands we ran: 
```
# cordon faulty node
kubectl cordon gpu-pool-27
# restart device plugin on node
kubectl -n kube-system logs daemonset/nvidia-device-plugin -l kubernetes.io/hostname=gpu-pool-27
kubectl -n kube-system delete pod -l name=nvidia-device-plugin --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-pool-27
```
sara: Thanks. I'll update the incident channel if anything else pops up. For now pausing autoscaler seems to have stopped additional churn. :eyes:
